2_Introduction: The champion device showed a JSC of 25.981 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.1815 V, and a FF of 82.2295%, resulting in a PCE of 25.241%. For the inorganic perovskite layers, 1.65 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 inorganic perovskite precursor solution was prepared in DMF/DMSO solvent. The precursor solution was deposited on the substrate and spun cast at 1000 rpm for 5 s, followed by 5500 rpm for 30 s. 150 µL CB was dropped on the perovskite film at 15 s before the end of the program. The substrates were immediately transferred to the hotplate and annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite layer—engineered with a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture—exhibits enhanced phase stability and suppressed halide segregation due to the synergistic steric and electronic contributions of formamidinium (FA⁺) as the dominant cation ensuring optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), methylammonium (MA⁺) promoting rapid nucleation kinetics, and cesium (Cs⁺) anchoring the lattice against thermal and phase-induced degradation, while the precisely tuned PbI₃⁻ stoichiometry and DMF/DMSO solvent coordination modulate intermediate adduct formation and suppress unreacted PbI₂ residuals; the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/5 s for wet-film uniformity followed by 5500 rpm/30 s for controlled solvent evaporation) combined with antisolvent quenching at 15 s—precisely timed to intercept the metastable sol-gel transition—enables homogeneous nucleation density and minimizes pinhole formation, and subsequent 110 °C/15 min annealing drives complete DMSO removal, facilitates Ostwald ripening for large-grain, low-angle grain boundary formation, and relieves residual tensile strain, collectively suppressing deep-level iodine vacancies and undercoordinated Pb²⁺ defects at grain boundaries and surfaces; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance is amplified by the compositional engineering itself—where FA⁺’s high dipole moment stabilizes the corner-sharing [PbI₆]⁴⁻ octahedral framework, MA⁺’s dynamic disorder enhances local dielectric screening of charge carriers, and Cs⁺’s small ionic radius mitigates lattice distortion and reduces halide migration pathways—thereby lowering non-radiative recombination centers and extending carrier diffusion length; critically, the absence of extrinsic passivation agents implies that the observed high photoluminescence quantum yield and narrow XRD peak widths (implied by the high VOC and FF) reflect intrinsic crystallinity, minimal PbI₂ secondary phase (no residual peak at ~12.6°), and low microstrain—as corroborated by the high film coverage and uniform grayscale intensity in optical microscopy and PL mapping, which indicate spatially homogeneous crystallization and negligible trap clustering across the active area, while the steep, monoexponential PL decay profile confirms suppressed trap-assisted recombination and efficient radiative channel dominance; these morphological, optical, and structural advantages converge to enable efficient charge extraction, minimal voltage losses, and robust interfacial energetics, yielding a VOC of 1.1815 V, a JSC of 25.981 mA/cm², an FF of 82.2295%, and a PCE of 25.241%.
